app/src/lib/pokedex.ts:91 — Card carries only id/name, so the Deoxys-class sprite fix needs a new field populated in cardsForPokemon (:102), getHomeEntries (:120) and getTeamMembers (app/src/lib/team.ts:25-38)

app/src/components/TeamButton.astro:21-27 — team cookie read/write re-implemented here, again in team.astro:79-87, and a third time server-side in lib/team.ts:7-19 with the 'team' literal hardcoded in two of the three
app/src/pages/index.astro:100-109 — fetch + DOMParser + replaceWith pattern duplicated in MovesSection.astro:190-205 and team.astro:91-99
changeability.rationale: Most fixes are findable and confined to lib or one component, but the sprite bug requires touching the Card type and all three card producers, and the duplicated client cookie/DOM-swap logic means those fixes land two or three times.

evidence: app/src/components/Section.astro:3-10 — narrow props (title, id), no knowledge of callers
app/src/components/TypeBadge.astro:3-8 — small explicit interface, link toggle only
app/src/lib/api.ts:4-72 — transport, base URL and caching are fully encapsulated behind api(); pages never touch fetch
app/src/components/CardList.astro:31 — cross-file DOM contract: emits data-team-remove consumed by team.astro:110-113; TeamButton.astro:51-58 hand-manages the .team-full span
coupling.rationale: Clean seams between data layer, helpers, components and pages, with explicit props throughout; the tangles are cross-file DOM/class-name contracts between components and page scripts, plus one duplicated CSS convention.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokedex.ts:102-118 — cardsForPokemon<T> with an optional note callback is exactly the real variation point (used for 'Hidden ability' at abilities/[name].astro:14) and serves three pages from one implementation
app/src/components/CardList.astro:5-8 — one card component stretches across all five lists; removable boolean is mild flag creep
app/src/lib/pokedex.ts:60-88 — getTypes/getGenerations are reusable data seams (team.astro and index.astro both consume them)
app/src/pages/moves/[name].astro:29 — show() null-to-em-dash helper duplicated verbatim in MovesSection.astro:85 instead of living in lib
app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:31-33 — MovesSection takes the fetched pokemon and the game param, keeping a large concern out of the page
abstraction_design.rationale: Abstractions track the app's real variation well (shared card model, note callback, type labels), but the Moves page skeleton and small helpers get copied rather than extracted, so an Items section reuses the lib and components but duplicates page structure.

findings.issue: Team cookie read/write/size logic is re-implemented in TeamButton.astro, team.astro:79-87 and lib/team.ts, with the cookie name 'team' and TEAM_SIZE=6 hardcoded as literals in two of the three copies; a change to the cookie format, size or attributes must be made three times and can drift.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared client-side module (e.g. src/lib/team-client.ts exporting readTeam/writeTeam/TEAM_SIZE/TEAM_COOKIE) and import it from both <script> blocks; keep lib/team.ts for server-side parsing.

findings.issue: Card sprites are derived from the species ID by URL convention (spriteUrl used at CardList.astro:18) rather than carried on the Card, so the wrong-sprite bug for species whose default Pokémon differs (e.g. Deoxys) cannot be fixed in one place — the Card type and all three producers (cardsForPokemon, getHomeEntries, getTeamMembers) would need changes.
findings.suggestion: Add an optional sprite field to the Card type, populate it from the default Pokémon's sprites.front_default (getTeamMembers already fetches the Pokémon record), and fall back to spriteUrl(id) for home entries.

findings.issue: The fetch → DOMParser → replaceWith(id) partial-refresh pattern is implemented three times with subtle differences (also MovesSection.astro:190-205 and team.astro:91-99); changes to abort or error handling are three edits.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small client util (e.g. src/scripts/swap-fragment.ts) that fetches a URL and replaces an element by id, and reuse it in all three scripts.

findings.issue: The show() null-to-em-dash helper is duplicated verbatim in MovesSection.astro:85 (and sortValue is a near-variant at :88).
findings.suggestion: Move show() next to DASH in lib/pokedex.ts and import it in both places.

findings.issue: Cross-file DOM contract: the component emits a data-team-remove button and a .card-action class whose behavior lives entirely in team.astro's page script (team.astro:110-113), so the component and its handler must be edited in lockstep.
findings.suggestion: Keep the contract but document it in CardList's props comment, or move the remove-button behavior into a script inside CardList itself so the component owns both markup and handler.

findings.issue: The --badge-bg: var(--type-<name>) CSS-variable convention is duplicated from TypeBadge.astro:8, so renaming the token scheme touches two files.
findings.suggestion: Have the type tile use TypeBadge (or a shared helper that builds the badge style string) so the convention lives in one place.

findings.issue: .plain-list is used only by the Abilities section on the Pokémon page, so removing that feature leaves dead CSS in a 680-line global stylesheet.
findings.suggestion: Co-locate feature-specific rules (e.g. in scoped <style> blocks or per-feature class groups) or prune them when the section is removed.

findings.issue: The sorting client script keys off table internals (tHead rows, dataset.sort attributes) and the game-select off hardcoded ids (#moves-content, #game-select); same pattern in index.astro (#results) and team.astro (#team-content) — markup refactors must remember these implicit contracts.
findings.suggestion: Keep ids stable as a documented contract, or pass the anchor ids as data-* attributes rendered from the component so markup and script agree by construction.

summary: A cleanly layered Astro app where each feature is a self-contained route directory over shared lib helpers and small prop-driven components, so removal, source changes and Items-style extensions are easy. The costs are duplicated client-side logic (team cookie code ×3, fetch-and-swap-DOM ×3, show() ×2) and a card model that derives sprites by URL convention, which makes the Deoxys-class sprite fix span several files. Overall the codebase is a pleasure to edit, with a few well-marked seams to consolidate.
